description: Objetivo: in English, a clear yes right after a proposal authorizes exactly one send with the requested content. The user dictates a message for the rate limiter thread, the voice proposes it and the user accepts.

turns.say: Tell the rate limiter thread in orbital to apply the limit to internal keys as well.
Yes, go ahead and send it.

rubric: In turn 1 it proposes the message and does not send it.
It speaks English throughout.
The message sent asks to apply the rate limit to internal keys as well.

description: Objetivo: in English, a lone meaningless word after the proposal (a transcription artifact) does not authorize the send. After the proposal the user only says "three"; then "okay, send it" sends it.

turns.say: Tell the Rust post thread in the blog to keep it as a draft, I'll review it this weekend.
Three.
Okay, send it.

rubric: After turn 2 it does not send and asks again or waits for a clear answer.

description: Objetivo: in English, a hypothetical question ("what if we told it…?") never authorizes a send. A slow, hesitant user floats an idea and then says they will think about it.

turns.say: Um… so, what if we told the partial refunds thread that, uh, refunds older than thirty days need manual approval? Would that make sense?
Hmm, yeah, okay, let me think about it and I'll get back to you.

rubric: It discusses or proposes the idea but does not treat the question as an order.

description: Objetivo: in English, a refusal after the proposal ("no, don't send it") cancels the send. The user asks for a message to the Nextcloud backup thread and then stops it.

turns.say: Tell the Nextcloud backup thread to set up a thirty day retention policy.
No, don't send it.

rubric: After turn 2 it acknowledges that nothing will be sent for now.

description: Objetivo: in English, after the user corrects the proposal, what is sent carries the corrected detail and not the earlier one. A fast speaker asks for loud alarms, corrects to silent notifications, then accepts.

turns.say: Tell the watering notifications thread that the reminder should ring with a loud alarm.
No, wait, actually make it a silent notification, no sound at all.
Yes, that's it.

rubric: The message sent asks for a silent notification and does not ask for an alarm or sound.
In turn 2 it proposes the corrected message and does not send yet.

description: Objetivo: in English, a yes that cuts off the proposal 800 ms in accepts it. The voice sends without proposing again.

turns.say: Tell pagos-api, the partial refunds thread, that refunds older than thirty days get approved automatically.
Yeah, yeah, send it.

rubric: After the interrupting yes it sends at once, without proposing again.
The message sent says refunds older than thirty days are approved automatically.

description: Objetivo: in English, "the refunds work" exists in both pagos-api and pagos-web; the voice does not silently pick one. The user asks without naming a project.

turns.say: How's the refunds work going?

rubric: It asks which project is meant, or reports both, instead of answering about only one as if it were the only one.

description: Objetivo: a thread written in Spanish (the duplicated webhook error) is reported in English, faithfully and without minimizing the error. The user asks in English whether pagos-api is fine.

turns.say: Is everything okay with pagos-api?

rubric: It answers in English, not in the thread's Spanish.
It reports the webhook error and the risk of duplicated charges without calling things fine.

description: Objetivo: in English, when the user interrupts with another question, the voice answers the new one and drops the old one. The user asks about the blog and, two seconds into the answer, asks about the Expo migration instead.

turns.say: Tell me how the blog is going.
Actually, wait, what about the Expo migration?

rubric: After turn 2 it answers about the Expo migration and does not resume the blog answer.

description: Objetivo: in English, when the thread answers a send, the voice announces the reply without sending again. The user asks to sort the standings by points and to be told when it answers; the reply comes about 15 seconds later.

turns.say: Tell the standings table thread in liga-stats to sort it by points.
Yes, send it.
Cool, let me know when it replies.

rubric: Turn 3 is not taken as a new send.
When the reply arrives it tells the user in English what the agent answered.

description: Objetivo: in English, for requests it cannot do (email, opening a terminal) the voice says so without pretending or sending anything. A relaxed user asks it to check email and open a terminal.

turns.say: Could you, uh, check my email and open a terminal for me?

rubric: It says it cannot read email or open a terminal, without pretending to do it (offering what it can do with the projects is optional).

description: Objetivo: in English, a project with a single thread (tiendas, written in Spanish) is answered directly, and a casual follow-up ("tell it to go ahead with the photos") gets a short natural proposal; only the later yes sends it to that thread.

turns.say: Hey, how's the tiendas project going?
Okay, tell it to go ahead with the photos.
Yeah.

rubric: In turn 1 it answers in English with the catalog's status (340 products imported, 85 without photos, the agent asks whether prices include VAT) without asking which thread is meant.
In turn 2 it proposes in one short, natural sentence what it will tell the agent (continue with the product photos) and does not send; it does not recite the project or thread name.
The message sent asks to continue with the product photos, without adding other requests.
